items.title: Bengaluru: Drunk IT employee held after allegedly firing air gun inside apt complex
items.summary: A 40-year-old IT professional has been taken into custody after allegedly opening fire with an air gun at security guards and parked vehicles inside an apartment complex near Anekal on the outskirts of Bengaluru in the early hours of Thursday. The incident occurred at Sipani Apartments near Bandapur in Anekal at around 2.45 am. The accused, identified as Anurag Tiwari, a native of Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, had been living in a rented flat at the complex for the past eight months and was employed at a private IT company in Whitefield. According to police, Tiwari was allegedly under the influence of alcohol and was speaking loudly on the phone and shouting inside his apartment. He later stepped onto the balcony and allegedly began firing pellets from an air gun. Police said the pellets struck several parked cars and the metal sheets covering the parking area, causing panic among residents who were awakened by the sound of gunfire. Security guards rushed to investigate after hearing the shots. However, Tiwari allegedly turned the air gun towards them and fired multiple rounds in their direction, forcing the guards to take cover. They then blew whistles to alert other residents and sought police assistance. According to investigators, the firing continued for nearly 45 minutes before personnel from the Surya Nagar Police Station reached the apartment complex and took Tiwari into custody. Police have seized the air gun and pellets allegedly used in the incident. No injuries have been reported. A case has been registered at the Surya Nagar Police Station, and further investigation is underway.

items.title: RSS chief says NEET concerns genuine, warns against branding Gen Z 'anti-national'
items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday, August 6, said that the grievances raised by students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak were genuine and cautioned against branding young protestors as "anti-national". His remarks come after weeks of police action against protesters and the eventual resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Defending the right to protest in a democracy, Bhagwat said the country's youth deserve dialogue because they represent the next generation. Speaking at a Gen Z-led event in Mumbai, Bhagwat said the concerns voiced by students reflected larger shortcomings in the country's education system. His remarks come in the wake of nationwide protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over alleged irregularities in national entrance examinations, during which protesters alleged police excesses and the Union government faced mounting criticism, culminating in Pradhan's resignation. "I'm saying, if Gen Z is protesting, they're not anti-national. They're our own people. They're our next generation. With this sense of belonging, along with dialogue, I said a sense of belonging is needed. A relationship is needed," Bhagwat said. Backing the concerns raised by the protesters, he added, "Whatever has happened, the grievance is genuine. There is a lot that needs to be done in Indian education; since it's not happening, it's being talked about." Bhagwat described protest as a legitimate democratic tool when other avenues of communication fail. "Protest is also a form of dialogue. We are sitting here and talking; if things are understood this way, it's fine. Otherwise, there will be a debate between us. If you are in some difficulty, or I am in some difficulty, and it is in your hands or my hands to resolve it, and it's not happening, then I will shout," he said. Drawing a contrast between generations, Bhagwat said today's youth were more willing to question authority than previous generations. "When we were at the age of Gen Z, the nature of our generation was such that we would accept what the elders said. We wouldn't question. Now Gen Z and Gen Alpha ask questions; they want logical answers," he said. He went on to praise younger generations, saying, "I feel this new generation, Gen Z, Gen Alpha, they are more honest than our existing generation," adding that "an honest appeal for patriotism and service works in them."
